newsitem.title: FRANCE: Casino softer after denies merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Casino softer after denies merger talks.

text.p: Casino fell back on Thursday after initially rising on the back of a denial by retailer Promodes it was in merger talks with the supermarkets group.
But traders said there was a lot of scepticism about the denial. "People take these denials with a pinch of salt especially after Axa's surprise move on UAP," said one trader.
"We've had the denial today which maybe has made the market a little more cautious but I think the majority of market participants expect that this deal will see the light of day."
At 1147 GMT, Casino was off 0.08 percent or 0.20 francs at 245.00 francs. Earlier, it touched a year high of 252.50 francs.
Casino's preference shares were off their best levels but still up 5.16 percent at 195.7 francs as the market bet they would get the same treatment as ordinary shares in a takeover.
Promodes was down 2.02 percent or 26 francs at 1,459 francs.

The business daily La Tribune reported on Thursday rumours Promodes was poised to make a one-for-six share paper offer for Casino. But Promodes isssued a statement saying it was not holding any kind of merger discussions with Casino.
Speculation about a merger has been rife for weeks amid talk of consolidation in the French food retail sector. On Wednesday, Casino gained 2.5 percent while Promodes lost 1.7 percent.
